mainTopic: Nullification of forbidden figs and of an egg that will become permitted later, the ברייתא 'it and its mother,' and eggs laid on back-to-back שבת and יום טוב (רב vs. רבי יוחנן, הכנה דרבה).
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a משנה about a ליטרא of forbidden figs pressed onto one of several fig-circles, where nobody knows which one. In רבי מאיר's version, רבי אליעזר says the figs are nullified and רבי יהושע requires one hundred tops. In רבי יהודה's version, רבי יהושע says they are never nullified, which is the opinion רב פפא relied on. רב פפא then explains the 'everyone agrees' case: we know the circle and only not the side. רב אשי gives a new reason why the earlier ברייתא's egg is never nullified: a doubt about יום טוב makes it a דבר שיש לו מתירין. Next, the גמרא discusses a ברייתא that says an egg 'may be eaten, it and its mother.' רבי זירא and אביי explain that the egg follows the hen, while רב מרי says the phrase is only a גוזמא. Then רב and רבי יוחנן argue about an egg laid on שבת or יום טוב that fall back to back. The גמרא explains that their argument is about הכנה דרבה and matches an earlier dispute of תנאים. Two stories follow. רב אדא בר אהבה forbids roasting an egg on the day it was laid. רב פפא postpones his answer until the next day, and his ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the top layers are nullified by the lower layers
steps.stepSummary: In רבי מאיר's version, רבי אליעזר says we treat the top fig-circles as separate pieces, and the lower circles nullify them.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי אליעזר] says: We view the upper ones as if they are separate pieces, and the lower ones nullify the upper ones.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of the quoted משנה. The word 'אומר' belongs to רבי אליעזר, as reported by רבי מאיר. He says the forbidden figs are nullified (בטל) by all the other figs, including those lower down in the containers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden ליטרא was pressed onto the top of one circle, so we might think only the other tops can nullify it. רבי אליעזר says we look at the upper layers as loose, separate pieces, so the lower layers also count toward nullifying them. This gives him plenty of permitted figs, so the forbidden ליטרא is easily בטל.

keyTerms.meaning: We view / we consider (a legal way of looking at something)
The upper ones (the top layers of figs)
Separate, loose pieces
The lower ones (the bottom layers of figs)
Nullify (literally 'raise up'), as in בִּיטּוּל of a forbidden mixture

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The speaker of 'אומר' is רבי אליעזר, quoted by רבי מאיר. He is not a new or unnamed speaker.

phrases.english: [Rabbi Eliezer] says: We view the upper ones
phrases.notes: We're still in the middle of the quote: 'רבי מאיר אומר, רבי אליעזר אומר.'

phrases.english: as if they are separate pieces,
and the lower ones nullify the upper ones.
phrases.notes: 'מעלות' means they cancel out the forbidden status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אומר: רואין את העליונות כאלו הן פרודות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה that the גמרא began quoting on the previous amud to support רב פפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי מאיר's version, רבי אליעזר holds that the upper figs count as separate pieces and are nullified by the lower figs.

steps.title: רבי יהושע in רבי מאיר's version: only one hundred tops can nullify
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the forbidden figs are nullified only if there are one hundred circle-tops. Otherwise all the tops are forbidden and the bottoms are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: If there are one hundred tops there, they are nullified. If not, the tops are forbidden and the bottoms are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside רבי מאיר's version, רבי יהושע gives a stricter view. Only the other tops count toward nullifying the forbidden figs, so you need one hundred of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע does not treat the top layers as loose pieces. Only other tops can nullify the forbidden top, and nullification needs a one-in-a-hundred ratio. Without that, every top is forbidden because any one of them could be the bad one. The bottoms stay permitted because the forbidden figs were only pressed on top.

keyTerms.meaning: Mouths / tops (of the fig-circles or containers)
They are nullified
Bottoms (the lower part of the containers)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ שָׁם מֵאָה פּוּמִּין — יַעֲלוּ,
phrases.english: If there are one hundred tops there, they are nullified,
phrases.notes: One part forbidden against one hundred parts permitted.

phrases.english: and if not, the tops are forbidden,
and the bottoms are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהושע אומר: אם יש שם מאה פומין יעלו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing, stricter view to רבי אליעזר's view in step 1, within רבי מאיר's version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי מאיר's version, רבי יהושע holds that nullification needs one hundred tops. Without that, the tops are forbidden and the bottoms are permitted.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version: רבי אליעזר holds the hundred-tops view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports the argument differently. In his version, the hundred-tops view belongs to רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: רבי אליעזר says, if there are one hundred tops there, they are nullified. If not, the tops are forbidden and the bottoms are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a second version of the argument, from רבי יהודה. In this version, the opinion that רבי מאיר gave to רבי יהושע is given to רבי אליעזר instead. This sets up a stricter opinion for רבי יהושע in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself is the same as in step 2: one hundred tops are needed, otherwise the tops are forbidden and the bottoms are permitted. What changed is who said it. Moving this view to רבי אליעזר leaves room for רבי יהושע to hold something even stricter.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says,
phrases.notes: Introduces a second version of who said what.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ שָׁם מֵאָה פּוּמִּין — יַעֲלוּ,
phrases.english: If there are one hundred tops there, they are nullified,
and if not, the tops are forbidden,
and the bottoms are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהודה אומר, רבי אליעזר אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of steps 1 and 2. רבי אליעזר now holds the view that רבי מאיר gave to רבי יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יהודה's version, רבי אליעזר requires one hundred tops for nullification. Otherwise the tops are forbidden and the bottoms are permitted.

steps.title: רבי יהושע in רבי יהודה's version: never nullified, even with three hundred
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יהודה's version, רבי יהושע says the forbidden figs are not nullified even among three hundred tops. This is the תנא that רב פפא was talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: Even if there are three hundred tops there, they are not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line the גמרא needed. רבי יהושע says this kind of item can never be nullified, no matter how many permitted pieces surround it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A circle of figs is sometimes sold by count, so it counts as an important item. רבי יהושע treats it as something that never becomes בטל, even at three hundred to one. This is exactly the opinion רב פפא pointed to: a תנא who holds that even 'something that is sometimes counted' is not nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: Three hundred
They are not nullified
An item that is sometimes counted / sold by unit (the background idea here)

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the proof for רב פפא's statement. It shows that one opinion treats an item that is only sometimes counted as never able to become בטל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ שָׁם שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת פּוּמִּין —
phrases.english: Even if there are three hundred tops there,
they are not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהושע אומר: אפילו יש שם שלש מאות פומין לא יעלו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהודה's version with רבי יהושע's strictest view. This is the actual source for רב פפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יהודה's version, רבי יהושע holds that the forbidden figs are never nullified, even among three hundred tops.

steps.title: Pressed into a circle, unknown which: everyone agrees it is nullified
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a case where the figs were pressed into an unknown circle. It says all opinions agree that they are nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he pressed it into a circle and does not know which circle he pressed it into, everyone agrees they are nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings another case and says it is not under dispute: the forbidden figs are nullified according to everyone. This line sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case sounds very much like the case the תנאים just argued about: forbidden figs pressed onto an unknown circle. Even so, the משנה says 'everyone' agrees that the figs are בטל. This claim of full agreement is what the גמרא is about to challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He pressed it (pressed the figs down)
A circle (a round cake or container of pressed figs)
Everyone agrees / according to all opinions

phrases.english: If he pressed it into a circle
and does not know into which circle he pressed it,
everyone agrees they are nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: דרסה בעגול ואינו יודע באיזה עגול דרסה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה continues with a case that it describes as agreed upon by all opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the figs were pressed into an unknown circle, all opinions agree they are nullified.

steps.title: How can everyone agree? This is the very case they argued about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by 'everyone agrees.' The case of figs pressed onto an unknown circle seems to be exactly what רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagreed about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees?! This is exactly their dispute!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording. How can it say 'everyone agrees' about a case that looks identical to the one the תנאים just argued over? רב פפא answers this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה, רבי יהושע (especially in רבי יהודה's version) held that the forbidden figs are not nullified. Yet this case also involves figs pressed onto an unknown circle, and the משנה claims unanimous agreement. The גמרא points out the contradiction, which forces it to explain how this case is different.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as / this is exactly
Their dispute

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning the law of nullification itself. It is questioning the משנה's wording 'דברי הכל.' The problem is that the case looks the same as the disputed case, so how can it be unanimous?

phrases.english: Everyone agrees?!
phrases.notes: Said in surprise, as a challenge.

phrases.english: This is exactly their dispute!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording 'דברי הכל' in step 5 by comparing it to the dispute in steps 1 through 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that 'everyone agrees' the figs are nullified in the case of pressing into an unknown circle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case seems identical to the case רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argued about. So it cannot be unanimous unless it differs in some way.

steps.title: רב פפא: they know which circle, but not which side
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers the challenge. In the 'everyone agrees' case, the person knows which circle the figs were pressed into, but not which side (north or south). Everyone agrees that this is nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what the משנה means. He pressed it into a circle, but he does not know where on that circle he pressed it, whether on its north side or its south side. In that case everyone agrees it is nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from Step 6. The 'everyone agrees' case is a different case from the one רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument was about a circle we cannot identify at all. Here we do know which circle the figs went into, but we cannot tell which part of it. When the forbidden piece has no known location, it loses its importance. So even the strict opinion agrees that it is nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means': reinterpreting a statement
He pressed it (the dried figs) into the circle
A round cake of pressed dried figs
Its north side / its south side
'They go up': they are nullified and permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In the argued case, we don't know WHICH circle. In this case, we know the circle and only do not know the SIDE of it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: This is what it means:
He pressed it onto a circle,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּאֵיזֶה מְקוֹם עִגּוּל דְּרָסָהּ,
phrases.english: but he does not know onto which place of the circle he pressed it,
whether on its north side or on its south side —
everyone agrees they are nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 6 by redefining the 'everyone agrees' case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case (אוקימתא): narrowing what the משנה's case means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Unknown circle' meant the same case that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a known circle but an unknown side. A piece with no identifiable location is nullified according to everyone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the circle is known but the side is not, everyone agrees the figs are nullified.

steps.title: רב אשי: the egg is a doubt about יום טוב, so it is never nullified
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the earlier ברייתא (an egg mixed with a thousand eggs makes them all forbidden) differently. The egg is a case of ספק יום טוב ספק חול. It will become permitted later, so it is a דבר שיש לו מתירין, and that is not nullified even for a rabbinic prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, the case is a doubt whether it was יום טוב or a weekday. That is something that will become permitted later. And anything that will become permitted later is not nullified, even when the prohibition is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers his own reason why the forbidden egg in the earlier ברייתא is not nullified. This replaces the explanation the גמרא gave before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we are lenient when we are unsure about a rabbinic law. But this egg will become fully permitted after יום טוב, so there is no reason to rely on nullification now. Just wait. That is why it is never nullified, even among a thousand.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really / actually': introduces a different explanation
Unsure whether it was יום טוב or a weekday
Something that will become permitted later on its own
With a rabbinic prohibition
Is not nullified

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a major rule: something that will become permitted later is not nullified, even in a mixture of a thousand.
steps.whatToRemember: דבר שיש לו מתירין is never nullified, not even when the prohibition is only rabbinic, because you can simply wait until it becomes permitted.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Actually,
a doubt whether it is a Festival or a weekday
is something that will become permitted,
phrases.notes: After יום טוב, the egg will be permitted.

phrases.english: and anything that will become permitted —
even with a rabbinic prohibition, is not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the figs discussion and returns to the egg ברייתא from earlier on the daf, giving a different explanation of it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative explanation of the earlier ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Earlier on the daf, the גמרא explained the ברייתא as dealing with the egg of a טריפה. That egg is a Torah prohibition and an item that is counted (דבר שבמנין), so it is not nullified.
steps.terutzMaskana: The egg is not nullified because it is a דבר שיש לו מתירין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that will become permitted later is not nullified, even with a rabbinic prohibition.

steps.title: A new teaching: the egg is eaten together with its mother
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אחרים in the name of רבי אליעזר: an egg laid on יום טוב may be eaten, it and its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: אחרים say in the name of רבי אליעזר: An egg may be eaten, it and its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. It says an egg laid on יום טוב may be eaten together with the chicken that laid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new section. The ברייתא gives a lenient ruling for the egg but does not explain what kind of chicken it means. That missing detail sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': a תנא quoted without a name
It may be eaten, it and its mother (the hen)

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Others say in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
An egg — it and its mother may be eaten.
phrases.notes: Speaking of an egg laid on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the nullification discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An egg laid on יום טוב may be eaten together with its mother.

steps.title: Which kind of chicken is this about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. If the chicken was meant for eating, the ruling is obvious. If it was meant for laying eggs, then both the egg and the chicken should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If it is a chicken set aside for eating, it is obvious that both it and its mother are permitted! If instead it is a chicken set aside for laying eggs, both it and its mother are forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the ברייתא against both possible kinds of chicken. Neither one fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chicken meant for eating is ready food, so its egg is permitted too, and there would be nothing new to teach. A chicken kept for eggs is מוקצה, since it was not meant to be eaten on יום טוב, and so its egg is forbidden as well. Either way, the ruling 'it and its mother may be eaten' seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say
It's obvious!
Set aside for eating
Set aside for laying eggs

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing?
If we say with a chicken set aside for eating —
it is obvious that it and its mother are permitted!
Rather, with a chicken set aside for laying eggs —
it and its mother are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ברייתא just quoted in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of chicken would make the ברייתא's ruling both new and correct?
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא 'the egg may be eaten, it and its mother'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible cases fail. A chicken for eating makes the ruling obvious, and a chicken for laying eggs makes both forbidden.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the egg is eaten because of its mother
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reads the ברייתא as: the egg is permitted 'along with' its mother. If the chicken itself is eaten on יום טוב, the egg is permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: The egg may be eaten because of its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא re-reads the words of the ברייתא. The egg's status depends on the mother's status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mean both are simply permitted. It means the egg follows the mother: if the mother is slaughtered and eaten, the egg is permitted too. This creates a case that is neither obvious nor impossible, but it still needs a clear example.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of / along with its mother

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It may be eaten because of its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: תֵּאָכֵל אַגַּב אִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 by re-reading the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The egg's permission depends on its mother being eaten.

steps.title: What would such a case look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a concrete case where the egg's status depends on whether the mother is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא asks for a real-life example of רבי זירא's idea, preparing for אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chicken is normally either for eating or for eggs, and we already saw that both of those fail. So we need a chicken whose purpose is not yet decided.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? / How does it look?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a concrete example of רבי זירא's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real case where the egg's status depends on whether the mother is eaten.

steps.title: אביי: a chicken bought with no stated purpose
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the case is a chicken bought without saying what it was for. If it is slaughtered, it becomes clear that it was meant for eating, and the egg is permitted. If it is not slaughtered, it becomes clear that it was meant for eggs, and the egg is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: For example, where he bought it without saying what it was for. If it was slaughtered, it becomes clear that it was meant for eating. If it was not slaughtered, it becomes clear that it was meant for laying eggs.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the concrete case. The chicken's purpose, and so the egg's status, is decided after the fact by what the owner does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the owner never said what the chicken was for, its purpose is open. What he does later, slaughtering it or not, shows looking back what its purpose was all along. This idea, that a later choice clarifies an earlier status, is called ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: He bought it without saying what it was for
It was slaughtered
It became clear (looking back)

steps.whatToRemember: The egg follows its mother. For a chicken bought with no stated purpose, slaughtering it shows looking back that it was food, so its egg is permitted. Not slaughtering it shows it was for eggs, so its egg is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: The chicken's status is not decided when the egg is laid. It is decided later, by what happens to the chicken, and that decision then reaches back to the past.

phrases.english: Abaye said: For example, where he bought it without specifying,
if it was slaughtered — it is clarified that it was set aside for eating.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִשְׁחֲטָה — הוּבְרְרָה דִּלְגַדֵּל בֵּיצִים עוֹמֶדֶת.
phrases.english: If it was not slaughtered — it is clarified that it was set aside for laying eggs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 with a concrete case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A chicken bought with no stated purpose. Whether it is slaughtered decides, looking back, what it was for, and so whether the egg is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a later action can decide an earlier legal status (ברירה). This idea comes up again in later discussions.

steps.title: רב מרי: The Phrase Is Just an Exaggeration
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי gives a different answer to the question of Step 10: 'it and its mother' is a גוזמא, not a literal ruling about the mother hen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: The ברייתא is using an exaggeration.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי offers a new way to read the ברייתא's strange words 'it and its mother.' He says they are not meant literally at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא and אביי read 'it and its mother' as a real legal link between the egg and the hen. רב מרי says the phrase is only a figure of speech, a way of saying 'this egg is completely permitted.' This removes the original problem of Step 10, because the ברייתא is no longer making any statement about the hen.

keyTerms.meaning: An exaggeration; a figure of speech that is not meant literally
It (the ברייתא) is teaching

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
It is teaching an exaggeration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to the question of Step 10, different from the readings of רבי זירא and אביי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'it and its mother' is a גוזמא, an emphatic way of saying the egg is surely permitted. It says nothing about the hen.

steps.title: Proof: The Full ברייתא Also Mentions 'a Chick and Its Shell'
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי cites a fuller version of the same ברייתא that adds 'and a chick and its shell,' to show the ברייתא uses exaggerated language.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: אחרים say in the name of רבי אליעזר: An egg may be eaten, it and its mother, and a chick and its shell.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי brings his evidence: the full ברייתא contains an extra phrase, 'a chick and its shell.' The next steps will show that this phrase cannot be literal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full ברייתא has two strange pairs: 'it and its mother' and 'a chick and its shell.' If רב מרי can show that the second pair is clearly an exaggeration, then the first pair, which sits in the same sentence, is an exaggeration too.

keyTerms.meaning: A chick
Its shell

phrases.english: As it is taught:
Others say in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
An egg may be eaten, it and its mother,
and a chick and its shell.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב מרי's claim
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא's phrase 'it and its mother' is a גוזמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fuller ברייתא, which adds the phrase 'and a chick and its shell'

steps.title: What Does 'Its Shell' Mean? Not a Real Shell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'its shell' means. It rules out a literal shell, because a shell is not food.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'its shell'? If you say it means an actual shell, is a shell something people eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the phrase 'a chick and its shell.' It first shows that it cannot mean eating the actual shell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling about what 'may be eaten' makes no sense for an eggshell, because nobody eats shells. So the literal reading fails, and the גמרא will look for another meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a possible reading that will be tested
Actual, literal
Fit for eating; edible

phrases.english: What is 'its shell'?
If you say an actual shell,
is a shell edible?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the extra phrase cited in Step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'its shell' in the ברייתא. The literal meaning is rejected because a shell is not edible.

steps.title: Second Attempt: A Chick Still Inside Its Shell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'and its shell' means 'in its shell,' that is, a chick that has not yet hatched.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a chick in its shell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second literal reading: the ברייתא permits eating a chick while it is still inside the egg. The next step will test this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading changes 'and its shell' into 'in its shell.' It would make the phrase a real halachic ruling: an unhatched chick may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: In its shell (that is, not yet hatched)

phrases.english: Rather, a chick in its shell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a new meaning after the literal shell was rejected
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Proposed reading: the ברייתא permits eating a chick that is still inside its shell.

steps.title: Rejected: Everyone Forbids an Unhatched Chick
steps.stepSummary: The 'in its shell' reading fails. The רבנן and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב argue only about a chick that has already hatched; everyone agrees that a chick still in its shell is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב only where the chick has come out into the open world. But where it has not come out into the open world, they do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the reading of Step 17. No תנא permits a chick that is still inside its shell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב permits a chick right after it hatches, and the רבנן forbid it. That argument applies only once the chick is out in the world. Inside the shell, everyone forbids it. So no ברייתא would permit 'a chick in its shell,' and this literal reading fails too.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree up to this point; the argument is limited to this case
The open air of the world; here, having hatched

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse רבי אליעזר (quoted by אחרים in the ברייתא) with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. They are two different תנאים.

phrases.english: The Rabbis disagree only
with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov
where it came out into the open world.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלֹא יָצָא לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם —
phrases.english: But where it did not come out into the open world,
they do not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'chick in its shell' reading proposed in Step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that the ברייתא permits an unhatched chick
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No opinion permits a chick that is still in its shell. The known dispute covers only a chick that has already hatched.

steps.title: Both Phrases Are Exaggerations
steps.stepSummary: Since 'a chick and its shell' cannot be literal, it must be a גוזמא. So 'it and its mother' in the same ברייתא is also a גוזמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'a chick and its shell' is an exaggeration. Here too, 'it may be eaten, it and its mother' is an exaggeration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes רב מרי's proof. Both strange phrases are just emphatic speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both literal readings of 'a chick and its shell' failed in Steps 16–18, so the phrase must be a figure of speech. The ברייתא clearly uses exaggerated language, so 'it and its mother' is exaggeration too. It only means the egg is fully permitted, and the question of Step 10 about the hen disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; applies the same logic to the other case

steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches to 'it and its mother.' רבי זירא and אביי read it literally: the egg follows the status of the hen (a hen bought without stated purpose, then slaughtered or not). רב מרי says it is only a גוזמא, an emphatic way of saying the egg is permitted. His proof is the matching phrase 'a chick and its shell,' which cannot be literal.

phrases.english: Rather, 'a chick and its shell' is an exaggeration;
here too, 'it may be eaten, it and its mother' is an exaggeration.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֶפְרוֹחַ וּקְלִיפָּתוֹ גּוּזְמָא, הָכָא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after both literal readings were rejected
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב מרי, 'it and its mother' is a גוזמא stressing that the egg is permitted. It is not a ruling about the hen.

steps.title: New Topic: Egg Laid on שבת or יום טוב When They Are Back-to-Back
steps.stepSummary: A dispute among אמוראים: when שבת and יום טוב fall on consecutive days, רב forbids an egg laid on one day from being eaten on the other, and רבי יוחנן permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: שבת and יום טוב (on consecutive days). רב said: If the egg was laid on this one, it is forbidden on that one. רבי יוחנן said: If it was laid on this one, it is permitted on that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion. It presents an argument between רב and רבי יוחנן about an egg laid on the first of two back-to-back holy days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is שבת followed by יום טוב, or the reverse. An egg laid on the first day is clearly forbidden that day. The question is whether it becomes permitted on the second day. רב says no, and רבי יוחנן says yes.

keyTerms.meaning: It was laid (born) on this day
Forbidden
Permitted

phrases.english: It was stated: Shabbat and Yom Tov (back-to-back),

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: נוֹלְדָה בָּזֶה — אֲסוּרָה בָּזֶה,
phrases.english: Rav said: laid on this one, it is forbidden on that one;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: נוֹלְדָה בָּזֶה — מוּתֶּרֶת בָּזֶה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan said: laid on this one, it is permitted on that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the previous discussion was concluded
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: an egg laid on שבת is forbidden on the following יום טוב, and vice versa. רבי יוחנן: it is permitted on the second day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute is the subject of the next several steps. It is also relevant every year when יום טוב falls right before or right after שבת.

steps.title: Does רב Treat the Two Days as One Holiness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that רב's reason is that he views שבת and יום טוב as one continuous holiness (קדושה אחת).
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב holds that it is one holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to search for the reasoning behind רב's ruling. This line sets up the next move, which will test this suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the two days count as one long holy day, an egg forbidden on the first day stays forbidden on the second. The wording 'shall we say' signals a suggestion that the גמרא may challenge or reject.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say; introduces a proposal that will be tested
He holds (as his view)
One single holiness; the two days count as one unit

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav holds:
It is one holiness?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא קָסָבַר רַב: קְדוּשָּׁה אַחַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the reasoning behind רב's ruling in Step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב's ruling rests on viewing שבת and יום טוב as one continuous קדושה

steps.title: רב himself holds that שבת and יום טוב are two separate holinesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proposal from Step 21. רב cannot hold that שבת and יום טוב are one holiness, because he rules like the ארבעה זקנים, who follow רבי אליעזר's view that they are two holinesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב say: The הלכה follows the four elders, who ruled according to רבי אליעזר, who said that שבת and יום טוב are two separate holinesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion that רב sees שבת and יום טוב as one continuous holiness. It quotes another ruling of רב that says the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 21 the גמרא suggested that רב forbids the egg because he sees both days as one holiness (קדושה אחת). However, רב rules elsewhere like רבי אליעזר that they are שתי קדושות, two separate holinesses. So רב's reason for forbidding the egg must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] say? This is a standard opening for a contradiction from someone's own words.
Four elders, a group of sages whose ruling רב adopted.
Two holinesses. שבת and יום טוב are each separate, not one long holy day.
One holiness. This is the view being rejected here as רב's reason.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:
The halacha is like the four elders
phrases.notes: They ruled about an עירוב when שבת and יום טוב are back to back.

phrases.english: who follow the view of Rabbi Eliezer,
who said: they are two separate holinesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reason for רב's view proposed in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proposal that רב holds שבת and יום טוב are קדושה אחת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own ruling elsewhere says they are שתי קדושות, so he cannot hold they are one holiness.

steps.title: The real argument is about הכנה דרבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new explanation. רב accepts הכנה דרבה, so a holy day cannot prepare an egg for another holy day. רבי יוחנן does not accept הכנה דרבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here they argue about רבה's 'preparation.' רב holds of הכנה דרבה, and רבי יוחנן does not hold of הכנה דרבה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the 'one holiness' explanation failed, the גמרא offers a different reason for the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן. They disagree about רבה's principle of הכנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה taught that an egg is fully formed the day before it is laid, so the previous day 'prepares' it. Food for שבת or יום טוב must be prepared on a regular weekday, not on another holy day. רב accepts this, so even though the days are two holinesses, the first holy day cannot prepare the egg for the second. רבי יוחנן rejects this principle, so he permits the egg.

keyTerms.meaning: רבה's preparation. A holy day may not prepare food for another holy day. Only a weekday may prepare it.
They argue about.
He holds of it / he does not hold of it.

steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation lets רב keep his view that the days are two holinesses. He still forbids the egg, but for a completely different reason.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב went back to 'one holiness.' He agrees the days are separate. The problem is only that one holy day 'prepared' the egg for the other.

phrases.english: Rather, here
they argue about Rabba's 'preparation':
Rav holds of Rabba's preparation,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לֵית לֵיהּ הֲכָנָה דְרַבָּה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan does not hold of Rabba's preparation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason from Step 21 with a new one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the real basis of the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether הכנה דרבה applies. רב accepts it and forbids the egg. רבי יוחנן rejects it and permits the egg.

steps.title: The same argument already existed among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן matches an earlier argument among תנאים. One ברייתא permits the egg on the next holy day. רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אליעזר says this is still argued between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute among תנאים: An egg laid on שבת may be eaten on יום טוב, and one laid on יום טוב may be eaten on שבת. רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי אליעזר: It is still a dispute. בית שמאי say it may be eaten, and בית הלל say it may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן is not new. It shows an earlier argument among תנאים that lines up with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view (תנא קמא) permits the egg on the second day, like רבי יוחנן. רבי יהודה says it is still a dispute: בית הלל forbid it, like רב, and בית שמאי permit it. So each אמורא has support from the תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute of תנאים. The אמוראים' argument matches an earlier one.
It is still a dispute. The ruling is not agreed on by everyone.
The school of שמאי. Here they are lenient and permit the egg.
The school of הלל. Here they are strict and forbid the egg.

steps.confusionAlert: Here בית שמאי is the lenient side. This fits their opinion in the משנה, where they permit an egg laid on יום טוב.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute among the Tannaim:
If it was laid on Shabbat, it may be eaten on Yom Tov;
if laid on Yom Tov, it may be eaten on Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
It is still a dispute,
for Beit Shammai say: it may be eaten,
and Beit Hillel say: it may not be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the argument explained in Step 23 is parallel to an earlier argument among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The argument between רב and רבי יוחנן about an egg moving from one holy day to the next.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the תנא קמא against רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אליעזר, who reports a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.whatToRemember: רב (forbids) = הכנה דרבה = בית הלל according to רבי יהודה. רבי יוחנן (permits) = no הכנה דרבה = the תנא קמא.

steps.title: The host asks about roasting יום טוב eggs for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The host of רב אדא בר אהבה had eggs laid on a יום טוב that came right before שבת. He asked if he could roast them now on יום טוב and eat them tomorrow on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה's host had eggs laid on יום טוב, and שבת came right after. He came to רב אדא and asked him: What about roasting them now and eating them tomorrow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that tests the rule in real life. This step is only the question; it sets up רב אדא's answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eggs are forbidden today on יום טוב because they were newly laid. The host hopes to roast them today, while cooking is still allowed, and eat them on שבת, when the 'newly laid' problem may no longer apply. Whether this works depends on the argument we just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: His host, the person he was staying with.
To roast them.
Now, today.
Tomorrow.

phrases.english: The host of Rav Adda bar Ahava
had these eggs
laid on Yom Tov, with Shabbat coming next.
He came before him and said to him:
What about roasting them now
and eating them tomorrow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theoretical argument to a practical case about eggs going from יום טוב to שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May eggs laid on יום טוב be roasted on יום טוב so they can be eaten on the שבת that follows?

steps.title: רב אדא: Even רבי יוחנן forbids the egg on its own day
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה tells his host that even if the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, the egg may only be eaten the next day. It may not be roasted or even handled on the day it was laid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What are you thinking? That in the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן, the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן? Even רבי יוחנן only allowed swallowing the egg on the next day. On the same day it was laid, he did not allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא answers his host's question. He says the host cannot roast the egg today, even according to the lenient view of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The host assumed that because רבי יוחנן permits the egg on the next holy day, he can prepare it now. רב אדא points out that רבי יוחנן's leniency only starts tomorrow. Today, the day it was laid, the egg is still forbidden, so roasting it now is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: What are you thinking? / What is your reasoning?
The practical ruling follows (a certain opinion)
To swallow it (raw, without cooking)
On its own day, the same day it was laid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן's leniency means the egg is fine right away. He only permits it on the NEXT day. On the day it was laid, it is still completely forbidden, even to roast for later.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets an important limit: arguing about whether the egg is allowed tomorrow says nothing about using it today.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your thinking?

phrases.aramaic: רַב וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן — הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: That between Rav and Rabbi Yochanan, the halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan?
phrases.notes: רב אדא spells out the assumption behind the host's question.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא קָא שָׁרֵי
phrases.english: Even Rabbi Yochanan did not permit
except to swallow it tomorrow,
but on its own day, no.
phrases.notes: On the day it was laid, the egg may not even be moved, so roasting it is certainly forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the host's question from Step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can eggs laid on יום טוב be roasted today and eaten on שבת?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Even רבי יוחנן only permits the egg on the next day; on its own day it is forbidden.

steps.title: A ברייתא: A freshly laid egg may not be moved at all
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב אדא. An egg laid on שבת or on יום טוב may not be moved that day for any use, even to cover a vessel or to prop up a bed leg.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: Whether an egg was laid on שבת or on יום טוב, one may not move it. One may not use it to cover a vessel, and one may not use it to prop up the legs of a bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב אדא's point. On the day an egg is laid, it may not be moved at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the egg may not even be moved for small, non-food uses like covering a pot, it certainly may not be roasted. This shows the egg is completely off-limits (מוקצה) on its own day, which is exactly what רב אדא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Moving or handling an object
The legs of a bed
An item set aside and forbidden to handle on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: And it was taught (in a baraita):
Both an egg that was laid on Shabbat
and an egg that was laid on a Festival —
one may not move it,
neither to cover a vessel with it,
nor to support the legs of a bed with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אדא's ruling in Step 26.
steps.raayaObject: רב אדא's claim that an egg is forbidden on the day it was laid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding moving an egg laid on שבת or יום טוב for any purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: Even by the lenient view, a newly laid egg is completely forbidden on its own day. The argument between רב and רבי יוחנן is only about the NEXT holy day.

steps.title: A man asks רב פפא about eggs laid on שבת before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A new story: רב פפא's host (or, some say, another man) had eggs laid on שבת and asked whether he could eat them the next day, on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא's host, and some say it was a certain man who came before רב פפא, had eggs that were laid on a שבת that came before a יום טוב. He came before him and said to him: May I eat them tomorrow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new, similar story. This time the eggs were laid on שבת, and the man only wants to eat them on יום טוב the next day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is exactly where רב and רבי יוחנן argue: an egg laid on one holy day, eaten on the next. Unlike רב אדא's host, this man is not asking to do anything today, only to eat the eggs tomorrow.

keyTerms.meaning: His host (the person whose house he stayed in)
What is the law? (asking a question)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa's host,
and some say, a certain man
who came before Rav Pappa.
He had these eggs
(laid) on Shabbat (that came before) a Festival.
phrases.notes: The eggs were laid on שבת, and יום טוב falls the next day.

phrases.english: He came before him and said to him:
May I eat them tomorrow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story testing the same argument between רב and רבי יוחנן, now only about eating on the next day.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May eggs laid on שבת be eaten on the יום טוב that follows?

steps.title: רב פפא postpones his answer until the next day
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא tells the man to come back tomorrow, because רב would not hold public teaching sessions across back-to-back holy days, out of concern about drunkenness. When the man returns, רב פפא begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go now and come back tomorrow. For רב would not set up an אמורא (a speaker who repeats the lecture to the crowd) over himself from one holy day to the next, because of drunkenness. When he came the next day, he said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא does not answer right away. He delays because of drunkenness on holy days, and the last line sets up his real answer, which comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People drank a lot of wine at holiday meals, so רב avoided giving public rulings on those days, because a ruling needs a clear head. רב פפא follows this and puts off the question. The final words, 'when he came the next day, he said to him,' open his actual ruling.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go now and come back tomorrow,
for Rav would not place a disseminator over himself
from one Festival day to the next
because of drunkenness.
phrases.notes: Wine at holiday meals could cloud the mind, so public rulings were avoided.
